question_text: Have you seen smoke, burning, or any sign of fire from the appliance?
explanation: Smoke or fire is a serious electrical and fire hazard.
guidance_text: Stop using the appliance immediately. If it is safe to do so, unplug it. If there is fire or smoke you cannot control, leave the area and call 000. Do not attempt DIY electrical repairs.

question_text: Is there a burning smell, melted plastic smell, or scorch marks?
explanation: Burning smells can indicate overheating wiring or components.
guidance_text: Stop using the appliance. If it is safe to do so, unplug it. Seek professional assessment. Do not open the appliance yourself.
source_name: Energy Safe Victoria — Using Electricity Safely

question_text: Have you seen sparks from the appliance, plug, or cord?
explanation: Sparking can indicate a dangerous electrical fault.
guidance_text: Stop using the appliance. If it is safe to do so, unplug it. Arrange professional assessment. Do not attempt DIY repairs.
source_name: Energy Safe Victoria — Using Electricity Safely

question_text: Does the appliance, plug, or cord become unusually hot during use?
explanation: Unusual heat can precede fire or electric shock hazards.
guidance_text: Stop using the appliance. If it is safe to do so, unplug it. Seek professional assessment.
source_name: Energy Safe Victoria — Using Electricity Safely

question_text: Have you felt a shock, tingling, or stinging when touching the appliance?
explanation: Electric shock risk means the appliance must not be used.
guidance_text: Stop using the appliance immediately. If it is safe to do so, unplug it. Seek professional assessment. Call 000 if someone is injured.
source_name: Energy Safe Victoria — Using Electricity Safely

question_text: Are there exposed wires, a damaged cord, or a damaged plug?
explanation: Damaged cords and exposed conductors are a shock and fire risk.
guidance_text: Stop using the appliance. If it is safe to do so, unplug it. Do not wrap or tape exposed wires as a DIY fix. Seek professional assessment.
source_name: Energy Safe Victoria — Using Electricity Safely

question_text: If the appliance has a battery, is it swollen, leaking, or damaged?
explanation: Damaged lithium batteries can overheat or catch fire.
guidance_text: Stop using the appliance and stop charging it. Do not puncture or crush the battery. If it is safe to do so, move it away from anything that can burn. Seek professional advice on safe handling and disposal, and never put batteries in household or recycling bins.
source_name: CFA Victoria — Victorian fire agencies urge caution over lithium-ion battery fire risks

question_text: Has liquid been spilled into the appliance, or has it been immersed in water?
explanation: Liquid and electricity together create a serious shock hazard.
guidance_text: Stop using the appliance. If it is safe to do so, unplug it. Do not switch it on to 'dry it out'. Seek professional assessment.
source_name: Energy Safe Victoria — Using Electricity Safely

question_text: Is there cracked casing, melted parts, or other serious visible damage?
explanation: Serious visible damage may expose live parts or indicate internal failure.
guidance_text: Stop using the appliance. If it is safe to do so, unplug it. Seek professional assessment.
source_name: Energy Safe Victoria — Using Electricity Safely

question_text: Does the appliance make unusual buzzing, popping, or grinding sounds?
explanation: Unusual sounds may indicate a fault; treat uncertain answers conservatively.
guidance_text: If you are unsure whether the sound is normal, stop using the appliance until a professional can assess it. This screening cannot confirm the appliance is safe.
source_name: Energy Safe Victoria — Using Electricity Safely

question_text: Does using this appliance repeatedly trip a circuit breaker or RCD/safety switch?
explanation: Repeated trips can indicate a serious electrical fault.
guidance_text: Stop using the appliance. Seek professional assessment. Do not keep resetting the breaker to force the appliance to run.
source_name: Energy Safe Victoria — Using Electricity Safely

question_text: Are you unsure about any of the warning signs above?
explanation: Uncertainty is treated conservatively in Iteration 1.
guidance_text: If you are unsure, treat the situation as uncertain and seek professional assessment. A 'No' to all listed signs does not mean the appliance is safe.
source_name: Energy Safe Victoria — Using Electricity Safely

question_text: Has FixForward or another source shown a possible recall that might affect this appliance?
explanation: A possible recall match is not a diagnosis. Only the official ACCC notice confirms whether your product is affected.
guidance_text: Follow the official ACCC recall notice for your product. Do not treat FixForward's possible match as confirmation. Official search: https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls

question_text: Could this appliance store personal data (for example accounts, Wi-Fi details, or usage history)?
explanation: Some connected appliances may hold personal information that should be removed before repair, sale, or disposal.
guidance_text: Where possible, sign out of accounts, wipe stored data using the manufacturer instructions, and remove any SIM or memory card before repair, sale or disposal. This is not legal advice and does not confirm that all data has been erased.
source_name: OAIC — Tips to protect your privacy
